title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: The Department of Manpower and Employment (DME), Small Enterprise Development Division (SEDD), National Enterprise Development Authority (NEDA) and National Craft Council (NCC) strengthened institutional-level coordination by agreeing with commercial banks (People's Bank, and Commercial Bank PLC), to provide financial assistance to start to returnees repatriated due to COVID-19 to start small businesses. SEDD, NEDA and NCC jointly developed a monitoring strategy for continuous monitoring and ensuring its sustainability. The Ministry of Labour & Foreign Employment (MOLFE) approved an updated training manual in 2022, available in three languages (English, Sinhala and Tamil), aimed at boosting the capabilities of Foreign Employment Development Officers (FEDO) and introducing them to international labour standards. The ministry also endorsed the implementation of five Operational Guidelines (Public Relations and Customer Service family development, plan, care plan, Migrant Labour Grievances, and Psychosocial First Aid), to enhance service delivery by FEDOs and their ability to protect migrant workers’ rights. A total of 222 FEDOs (77 women) were capacitated as master trainers using the newly adapted manual and guidelines to help empower FEDOs and improve the quality of services they provide to migrant workers. With the support of the Government of Japan, 539 (402 Female, 137 Males) Officers from DME, SEDD, NEDA and NCC have been supported with SME capacity-building training jointly delivered by ILO and Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) The initial training manual, which was initially created with the support of the ILO in 2018, has been revised and updated to address the evolving training needs within the current context. The Ministry of Labour & Foreign Employment has received technical assistance from the ILO in this endeavour. Furthermore, the ILO extended its technical expertise to assist the ministry in the development of operational manuals, designed to enhance the efficiency of service delivery in the field. The training support was provided by ILO through the assistance of HELVETAS Swiss Incorporation, the partner in promoting safe labour migration training.

title.narrative: 7.5.2. Number of Member States with new or improved services to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour and Foreign Employment conducted 3 tripartite-level validations on Sri Lanka's National Labour Migration Policy. The new policy with an action plan for 2023-2027 was approved by the Cabinet of Ministers in September 2023. The policy aligns with international labour standards, promoting governance of labour migration to provide decent and productive employment, secure rights and protection of migrant workers and ensure the well-being of their families, promote employment opportunities for skilled and semi-skilled migrant workers in local and global economies and enhance benefits of migration and its nexus with national development. The Digital Knowledge Hub (KH) platform to facilitate the dissemination of evidence-based knowledge for policy dialogues among a wide range of interested stakeholders was created and tested in August 2023. As part of this initiative, existing knowledge products were successfully uploaded to the repository section of the platform. Furthermore, the KH is equipped with a robust Learning Management System (LMS) designed to support the continued enhancement of government officers' capabilities to protect migrant workers. In addition, work is ongoing to actively invest in the development of human resources dedicated to the KH, and to creating new knowledge products by filling the knowledge gaps to further enrich the platform's offerings. Throughout the review and revision process of the NPME, the ILO with the support of the Government of Switzerland, played a pivotal role in offering technical support to the Ministry of Labour and Foreign Employment. A comprehensive evaluation of the NLMP 2008's implementation, conducted through evidence-based consultations involving migrant workers, their families, social partners, and other stakeholders, was facilitated to identify the policy gaps. The other key supports encompassed several key aspects, including 1. Facilitating policy dialogues and consultations to generate substantive evidence. 2. Integrating both national and international standards into the policy framework. 3. Compiling and drafting the resultant evidence-based policy and accompanying action plan. 4. Facilitating a series of validation sessions with the high-level Labour Migration Advisory Committee. The ILO, with the support of the Government of Switzerland and in collaboration with an external service provider, spearheaded the development of the KH platform, which includes the LMS too. This platform has been instrumental in summarizing and uploading existing knowledge products. Moreover, to bridge any existing knowledge gaps, new research initiatives have been commissioned. In line with the commitment to continuous improvement, ILO is creating new virtual courses to further enrich the platform's offerings focusing on Care & Family Development Plan 2. Grievance handling 3. Psychosocial First Aid Practice 4. Public relations and customer service. ILO is investing in the capacity building of government human resources to ensure the sustained and long-term maintenance of the KH. It will be handed over to the government before the end of 2023.
